title: Where Do Leadership Instincts Come From
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece challenges the common assumption that great leaders simply have innate instincts, arguing instead that what looks like instinct is really the combination of accumulated experience and clearly held values. Experience alone lets a leader recognize familiar patterns, but it is values that determine which patterns matter and how to act on them. The author describes this as a largely subconscious process, which is why it feels effortless and mysterious from the outside. Leaders who want to sharpen this ability, the piece argues, should focus deliberately on clarifying their values and seeking out more meaningful experience rather than waiting for some innate gift to appear.
points: What looks like leadership 'instinct' is really a combination of past experience and core values.
Values determine what matters most in a situation; experience supplies the pattern recognition.
The process happens largely subconsciously, which is why quick, confident judgments look effortless.
Leaders can deliberately improve by clarifying their values and seeking richer experience over time.
quotes: In our estimation, they seem to know things we wouldn’t expect them to know.
Decisions steeped in values can never be fully wrong, and the best leaders know that; therefore, they apply them religiously to every judgment and decision they encounter.
When leaders combine deep, past experience with core values, something magical happens. They operate from what looks like instinct.
We often refer to highly effective leaders, especially those with less experience or background, as having great leadership instincts.
More importantly, these people land on a good or right answer seemingly without much effort.
They are instinctively good at leadership, or so we believe.
Technically speaking, an instinct is an intuitive way of assessing and acting on a situation or problem.
Instincts are thought to be baked into the biology, family history, and personality of those who possess them.
